newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday November 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday November 29.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Majority parties reached an agreement over the controversial Euro-tax, raising the tax threshold for the self-employed to 16.5 million lire from 15.2 million. Foreign minister and leader of Italian Renewal party Lamberto Dini had fiercely criticised the one-off measure (all).

* Leader of the PDS, the largest party in the centre-left government coalition, Massimo D'Alema says the creation of a commission to carry on constitutional reforms should be accelerated and receive parliamentary approval by the end of the year. Otherwise the ruling coalition will propose its own reforms. But opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi wants to delay the discussions until January 15 (all).
* A Turin magistrate said Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti and finance director Francesco Paolo Mattioli would stand trial for alleged balance sheet falsificatiopn on January 15 (all).

* Speaking in Florence, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said Italy would not face any discrimination when it came to an assessment of the criteria for joining Europe's single currency but it could not expect any privileges either (all).
* Prime minister Romano Prodi says the Italian economy is under recovery and will not be slowed down by the new ERM central parity at 990 lire per mark (all).

* There will be no parliamentary inquiry into information technology group Olivetti, as requested by the Freedom Alliance. Ex-Olivetti chairman Carlo De Benedetti speaking to a parliamentary committee warned of the worsening crisis at the loss-making company. "The climate that has been created around Olivetti is perhaps the most serious threat weighing on thousands (of workers)" he said (all).
* Gemina shareholders approved by a wide majority a plan to spin off the holding company's industrial assets into a new company called Holding Partecipazioni Industriali (HPI) (all).
-- Financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore was not available today.
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
